manifest.title: Bounded Twin-Width Refinement of Triangulations

inputs.abstract:
Every generalized triangulation of a $d$-manifold with $n$ top-dimensional simplices admits a refinement whose dual graph has twin-width at most $4$. For $d\ge 1$, insert a stack of $s=2\lceil\log_2 n\rceil-1$ pillows at each face gluing, taking $s=0$ for $n\le 1$. With $m$ gluings the refinement has exactly $n+2sm$ simplices, hence at most $n+(d+1)ns$. This gives size $O(dn\log n)$ for $d\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2$. In this range a shorter stack also gives the bound $2dn\log_2 n$ from the abstract. For $n\le5$ or $d=1$, the original triangulation already has dual twin-width at most $4$.

The construction gives a homeomorphism of quotient realizations. The contraction sequence routes the subdivided dual edges through a binary tree. It applies to triangulations with boundary, multiple face gluings between the same simplices, and gluings within a simplex.

concepts.title: Generalized triangulations and their dual graphs
concepts.description:
Take finitely many copies of the standard $d$-simplex. Each gluing identifies
two distinct facet occurrences by a permutation of their vertices. A facet
occurs in at most one gluing. Unpaired facets give boundary, and two facets
of the same simplex may be paired. The realization carries the quotient
topology. The dual multigraph has one vertex per simplex and one edge per
gluing. Its adjacency relation on distinct vertices records the support of
the black edges used in a contraction sequence.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.StdSimplex
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
import Mathlib.Topology.Constructions.SumProd

/-!
---
title: Generalized triangulations and their dual graphs
type: definition
---
Take finitely many copies of the standard $d$-simplex. Each gluing identifies
two distinct facet occurrences by a permutation of their vertices. A facet
occurs in at most one gluing. Unpaired facets give boundary, and two facets
of the same simplex may be paired. The realization carries the quotient
topology. The dual multigraph has one vertex per simplex and one edge per
gluing. Its adjacency relation on distinct vertices records the support of
the black edges used in a contraction sequence.
-/

namespace Lax919488.FacePairings

abbrev Corner (d : ℕ) := Fin (d+1)
abbrev Simplex (d : ℕ) := stdSimplex ℝ (Corner d)

/-- A side of a gluing. Its frame sends the reference facet opposite 0
to the chosen facet of the cell. -/
structure Side (d : ℕ) (V : Type) where
  cell : V
  frame : Equiv.Perm (Corner d)

def Side.port {d : ℕ} {V : Type} (s : Side d V) := (s.cell, s.frame 0)

/-- The two sides of each gluing are indexed by false and true. -/
structure Diagram (d : ℕ) (V E : Type) where
  side : E → Bool → Side d V

def Diagram.IsPairing {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective fun p : E × Bool => (T.side p.1 p.2).port

/-- Reindex the barycentric coordinates by a vertex permutation. -/
def reindex {d : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Corner d)) (x : Simplex d) : Simplex d :=
  ⟨fun i => x.val (σ.symm i), fun _ => x.property.1 _, (σ.symm.sum_comp _).trans x.property.2⟩

inductive Diagram.Gluing {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) :
    (V × Simplex d) → (V × Simplex d) → Prop
  | face (e : E) (x : Simplex d) (onFace : x.val 0 = 0) :
      T.Gluing ((T.side e false).cell, reindex (T.side e false).frame x)
        ((T.side e true).cell, reindex (T.side e true).frame x)

/-- The quotient of the disjoint union of closed geometric simplices. -/
abbrev Diagram.Realization {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) := Quot T.Gluing

instance {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) : TopologicalSpace T.Realization :=
  letI : TopologicalSpace V := ⊥
  inferInstanceAs (TopologicalSpace (Quot T.Gluing))

def Diagram.chart {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) (v : V) (x : Simplex d) :
    T.Realization := Quot.mk _ (v,x)

def Diagram.dual {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) : SimpleGraph V where
  Adj u v := u ≠ v ∧ ∃ e b, (T.side e b).cell = u ∧ (T.side e (!b)).cell = v
  symm := by
    constructor
    rintro u v ⟨ne,e,b,hu,hv⟩
    exact ⟨ne.symm,e,!b,hv,by simpa using hu⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun _ h => h.1 rfl⟩

/-- A homeomorphism of realizations under which every new characteristic
map embeds into a model simplex of the original triangulation. -/
def Diagram.Refines {d : ℕ} {V E W F : Type} (U : Diagram d W F) (T : Diagram d V E) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : U.Realization ≃ₜ T.Realization, ∀ w, ∃ v, ∃ f : C(Simplex d, Simplex d),
    Topology.IsClosedEmbedding f ∧ ∀ x, h (U.chart w x) = T.chart v (f x)

end Lax919488.FacePairings

concepts.title: Twin-width of a dual multigraph
concepts.description:
The initial black multiplicity between two cells counts the face gluings
joining them, including loops. When two parts merge, each surviving part
has a black edge to the new part if it had a black edge to both old parts.
It has no edge if it had no edge to either. Every other case gives one red
edge. Edges between surviving parts keep their multiplicities. The width is
the maximum red degree, counting red edges with multiplicity.

A contraction sequence for the simple adjacency graph lifts to a sequence
of the same width for the dual multigraph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax919488.FacePairings
import Lax228581.TwinWidth

/-!
---
title: Twin-width of a dual multigraph
type: theorem
---
The initial black multiplicity between two cells counts the face gluings
joining them, including loops. When two parts merge, each surviving part
has a black edge to the new part if it had a black edge to both old parts.
It has no edge if it had no edge to either. Every other case gives one red
edge. Edges between surviving parts keep their multiplicities. The width is
the maximum red degree, counting red edges with multiplicity.

A contraction sequence for the simple adjacency graph lifts to a sequence
of the same width for the dual multigraph.
-/

namespace Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth

open FacePairings Lax228581.TwinWidth

noncomputable section

def edgeMultiplicity {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype E] (T : Diagram d V E) (u v : V) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter fun e =>
    ∃ b, (T.side e b).cell = u ∧ (T.side e (!b)).cell = v).card

structure Entry where
  black : ℕ
  red : ℕ
  deriving DecidableEq

def combine (a b : Entry) : Entry :=
  if 0 < a.black ∧ 0 < b.black then ⟨1,0⟩
  else if a = ⟨0,0⟩ ∧ b = ⟨0,0⟩ then ⟨0,0⟩ else ⟨0,1⟩

structure ContractionSequence {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype V] [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V]
    (T : Diagram d V E) (k : ℕ) where
  steps : ℕ
  parts : ℕ → Finset (Finset V)
  edges : ℕ → Finset V → Finset V → Entry
  symmetric : ∀ i A B, edges i A B = edges i B A
  initial : parts 0 = singletonPartition V
  initialEdges : ∀ u v, edges 0 {u} {v} = ⟨edgeMultiplicity T u v,0⟩
  final : (parts steps).card ≤ 1
  merge : ∀ i < steps, ∃ A ∈ parts i, ∃ B ∈ parts i, A ≠ B ∧
    let rest := ((parts i).erase A).erase B
    let C := A ∪ B
    parts (i+1) = insert C rest ∧ edges (i+1) C C = ⟨0,0⟩ ∧
    (∀ D ∈ rest, edges (i+1) C D = combine (edges i A D) (edges i B D)) ∧
    ∀ D ∈ rest, ∀ F ∈ rest, edges (i+1) D F = edges i D F
  width : ∀ i ≤ steps, ∀ A ∈ parts i, ∑ B ∈ parts i, (edges i A B).red ≤ k

def WidthAtMost {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype V] [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V]
    (T : Diagram d V E) (k : ℕ) : Prop := Nonempty (ContractionSequence T k)

axiom lift_sequence {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype V] [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V]
    (T : Diagram d V E) {k : ℕ} (h : HasTwinWidthAtMost T.dual k) : WidthAtMost T k

end
end Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth

statements.signature:
lift_sequence : ∀ {d : Nat} {V E : Type} [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : Fintype E] [inst_2 : DecidableEq V]
  (T : Lax919488.FacePairings.Diagram d V E) {k : Nat},
  Lax228581.TwinWidth.HasTwinWidthAtMost T.dual k → Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth.WidthAtMost T k

concepts.title: Realization of the stacked pillow refinement
concepts.description:
In positive dimension, inserting any finite stack of pillows at every
gluing preserves the quotient space. Under the homeomorphism, each new
simplex embeds as a closed subset of an original model simplex. The empty
stack works in every dimension.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax919488.StackedPillows

/-!
---
title: Realization of the stacked pillow refinement
type: theorem
---
In positive dimension, inserting any finite stack of pillows at every
gluing preserves the quotient space. Under the homeomorphism, each new
simplex embeds as a closed subset of an original model simplex. The empty
stack works in every dimension.
-/

namespace Lax919488.PillowSubdivision

open FacePairings StackedPillows

variable {d n m : ℕ} (T : Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m))

axiom pillow_refinement (s : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d ∨ s = 0) (h : T.IsPairing) :
  (refine T s).IsPairing ∧ (refine T s).Refines T

end Lax919488.PillowSubdivision

statements.signature:
pillow_refinement : ∀ {d n m : Nat} (T : Lax919488.FacePairings.Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m)) (s : Nat),
  Or (instLTNat.lt 0 d) (Eq s 0) →
    T.IsPairing → And (Lax919488.StackedPillows.refine T s).IsPairing ((Lax919488.StackedPillows.refine T s).Refines T)

concepts.title: Contraction sequence for the refined dual graph
concepts.description:
Replace each dual edge by the path through its pillow simplices. The
underlying simple graph has a contraction sequence of width at most $4$
when the stack has $2\lceil\log_2 n\rceil-1$ pillows. For $n\le1$ or $d=0$,
the trivial refinement suffices. Zipping the two vertices of each pillow
directly onto the tree gives the same bound with the shorter stacks.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax919488.StackedPillows
import Lax228581.TwinWidth

/-!
---
title: Contraction sequence for the refined dual graph
type: theorem
---
Replace each dual edge by the path through its pillow simplices. The
underlying simple graph has a contraction sequence of width at most $4$
when the stack has $2\lceil\log_2 n\rceil-1$ pillows. For $n\le1$ or $d=0$,
the trivial refinement suffices. Zipping the two vertices of each pillow
directly onto the tree gives the same bound with the shorter stacks.
-/

namespace Lax919488.RefinedDual

open FacePairings StackedPillows

variable {d n m : ℕ} (T : Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m))

axiom dual_width (h : T.IsPairing) :
  Lax228581.TwinWidth.HasTwinWidthAtMost (refine T (depth d n)).dual 4

/-- The same routing works with one pillow per level of the binary tree. -/
axiom short_dual_width (h : T.IsPairing) :
  Lax228581.TwinWidth.HasTwinWidthAtMost (refine T (shortLayers d n)).dual 4

end Lax919488.RefinedDual

concepts.title: Bounded twin-width refinement of triangulations
concepts.description:
Every generalized triangulation of a $d$-manifold $M$ with $n$ top-dimensional
simplices has a refinement of $M$ whose dual multigraph has twin-width at
most $4$. For $d\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, its size is $O(dn\log_2 n)$. The proof
constructs the refinement for any finite face pairing, so $M$ can be any
space homeomorphic to its realization. A second choice of stack length
gives at most $2dn\log_2 n$ simplices for $d\ge1$, $n\ge2$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax919488.PillowSubdivision
import Lax919488.RefinementSize
import Lax919488.RefinedDual
import Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth

/-!
---
title: Bounded twin-width refinement of triangulations
type: theorem
---
Every generalized triangulation of a $d$-manifold $M$ with $n$ top-dimensional
simplices has a refinement of $M$ whose dual multigraph has twin-width at
most $4$. For $d\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, its size is $O(dn\log_2 n)$. The proof
constructs the refinement for any finite face pairing, so $M$ can be any
space homeomorphic to its realization. A second choice of stack length
gives at most $2dn\log_2 n$ simplices for $d\ge1$, $n\ge2$.
-/

namespace Lax919488.RefinementBounds

open FacePairings StackedPillows MultigraphTwinWidth

/-- Theorem 1 with the explicit refinement from equation (1). -/
axiom bounded_twin_width_refinement {d n m : ℕ} (T : Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m))
    {M : Type} [TopologicalSpace M] (h : T.IsPairing) (realizes : Nonempty (T.Realization ≃ₜ M)) :
    let s := depth d n
    let U := refine T s
    let N := Fintype.card (Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) s)
    U.IsPairing ∧ U.Refines T ∧ Nonempty (U.Realization ≃ₜ M) ∧
      N ≤ n + (d+1)*n*layers n ∧
      (1 ≤ d → 2 ≤ n → (N : ℝ) ≤ 7 * d * n * Real.logb 2 n) ∧ WidthAtMost U 4

/-- The leading constant in the abstract for the nondegenerate range. -/
axiom two_d_refinement {d n m : ℕ} (T : Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m))
    {M : Type} [TopologicalSpace M] (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (h : T.IsPairing) (realizes : Nonempty (T.Realization ≃ₜ M)) :
    let s := shortLayers d n
    let U := refine T s
    U.IsPairing ∧ U.Refines T ∧ Nonempty (U.Realization ≃ₜ M) ∧
      (Fintype.card (Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) s) : ℝ) ≤ 2 * d * n * Real.logb 2 n ∧ WidthAtMost U 4

end Lax919488.RefinementBounds

statements.signature:
bounded_twin_width_refinement : ∀ {d n m : Nat} (T : Lax919488.FacePairings.Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m)) {M : Type} [inst : TopologicalSpace M],
  T.IsPairing →
    Nonempty (Homeomorph T.Realization M) →
      let s := Lax919488.StackedPillows.depth d n;
      let U := Lax919488.StackedPillows.refine T s;
      let N := Fintype.card (Lax919488.StackedPillows.Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) s);
      And U.IsPairing
        (And (U.Refines T)
          (And (Nonempty (Homeomorph U.Realization M))
            (And
              (instLENat.le N
                (instHAdd.hAdd n
                  (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd d 1) n) (Lax919488.StackedPillows.layers n))))
              (And
                (instLENat.le 1 d →
                  instLENat.le 2 n →
                    Real.instLE.le N.cast
                      (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 7 d.cast) n.cast) (Real.logb 2 n.cast)))
                (Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth.WidthAtMost U 4)))))
statements.doc: Theorem 1 with the explicit refinement from equation (1).

statements.signature:
two_d_refinement : ∀ {d n m : Nat} (T : Lax919488.FacePairings.Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m)) {M : Type} [inst : TopologicalSpace M],
  instLENat.le 1 d →
    instLENat.le 2 n →
      T.IsPairing →
        Nonempty (Homeomorph T.Realization M) →
          let s := Lax919488.StackedPillows.shortLayers d n;
          let U := Lax919488.StackedPillows.refine T s;
          And U.IsPairing
            (And (U.Refines T)
              (And (Nonempty (Homeomorph U.Realization M))
                (And
                  (Real.instLE.le (Fintype.card (Lax919488.StackedPillows.Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) s)).cast
                    (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 2 d.cast) n.cast) (Real.logb 2 n.cast)))
                  (Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth.WidthAtMost U 4))))

concepts.title: Size of the refinement
concepts.description:
With $n$ simplices and $m$ face gluings, inserting $s$ pillows at each
gluing gives $n+2sm$ simplices. Counting facet occurrences gives
$2m\le(d+1)n$. For $d\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, the resulting bound in equation (2)
is at most $7dn\log_2 n$. With the shorter stacks the estimate improves
to $2dn\log_2 n$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax919488.StackedPillows
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Base

/-!
---
title: Size of the refinement
type: theorem
---
With $n$ simplices and $m$ face gluings, inserting $s$ pillows at each
gluing gives $n+2sm$ simplices. Counting facet occurrences gives
$2m\le(d+1)n$. For $d\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, the resulting bound in equation (2)
is at most $7dn\log_2 n$. With the shorter stacks the estimate improves
to $2dn\log_2 n$.
-/

namespace Lax919488.RefinementSize

open FacePairings StackedPillows

variable {d n m : ℕ} (T : Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m))

axiom size_bound (s : ℕ) (h : T.IsPairing) :
  Fintype.card (Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) s) = n + 2*s*m ∧
  n + 2*s*m ≤ n + (d+1)*n*s

axiom logarithmic_bound (d n : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
  ((n + (d+1)*n*layers n : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 7 * d * n * Real.logb 2 n

/-- Size bound from the abstract using the shorter stacks. -/
axiom short_size (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (h : T.IsPairing) :
  (Fintype.card (Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) (shortLayers d n)) : ℝ) ≤ 2 * d * n * Real.logb 2 n

end Lax919488.RefinementSize

statements.signature:
logarithmic_bound : ∀ (d n : Nat),
  instLENat.le 1 d →
    instLENat.le 2 n →
      Real.instLE.le
        (instHAdd.hAdd n (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd d 1) n) (Lax919488.StackedPillows.layers n))).cast
        (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 7 d.cast) n.cast) (Real.logb 2 n.cast))

short_size : ∀ {d n m : Nat} (T : Lax919488.FacePairings.Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m)),
  instLENat.le 1 d →
    instLENat.le 2 n →
      T.IsPairing →
        Real.instLE.le
          (Fintype.card (Lax919488.StackedPillows.Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) (Lax919488.StackedPillows.shortLayers d n))).cast
          (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 2 d.cast) n.cast) (Real.logb 2 n.cast))
statements.doc: Size bound from the abstract using the shorter stacks.

statements.signature:
size_bound : ∀ {d n m : Nat} (T : Lax919488.FacePairings.Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m)) (s : Nat),
  T.IsPairing →
    And
      (Eq (Fintype.card (Lax919488.StackedPillows.Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) s))
        (instHAdd.hAdd n (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 2 s) m)))
      (instLENat.le (instHAdd.hAdd n (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 2 s) m))
        (instHAdd.hAdd n (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd d 1) n) s)))

concepts.title: Stacked pillow refinement
concepts.description:
Insert $s$ pillows at each face gluing. Each pillow consists of two
$d$-simplices paired along the $d$ facets containing vertex $0$. Their
opposite facets attach to their two neighbors. Seam $j$ is the gluing after
the first $j$ pillows. The two end seams use the frames of the old gluing.
With $s=0$ the construction recovers the original face pairings.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax919488.FacePairings
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

/-!
---
title: Stacked pillow refinement
type: definition
---
Insert $s$ pillows at each face gluing. Each pillow consists of two
$d$-simplices paired along the $d$ facets containing vertex $0$. Their
opposite facets attach to their two neighbors. Seam $j$ is the gluing after
the first $j$ pillows. The two end seams use the frames of the old gluing.
With $s=0$ the construction recovers the original face pairings.
-/

namespace Lax919488.StackedPillows

open FacePairings

abbrev Cell (V E : Type) (s : ℕ) := V ⊕ (E × Fin (2*s))
abbrev Joint (d : ℕ) (E : Type) (s : ℕ) := E × (Fin (s+1) ⊕ (Fin s × Fin d))

def leftHalf {s : ℕ} (j : Fin s) : Fin (2*s) := ⟨2*j.val, by omega⟩
def rightHalf {s : ℕ} (j : Fin s) : Fin (2*s) := ⟨2*j.val+1, by omega⟩

def originalSide {d s : ℕ} {V E : Type} (a : Side d V) : Side d (Cell V E s) :=
  ⟨.inl a.cell, a.frame⟩

def seam {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) (s : ℕ) (e : E) (j : Fin (s+1)) :
    Bool → Side d (Cell V E s)
  | false => if h : j.val = 0 then originalSide (T.side e false)
      else ⟨.inr (e,rightHalf ⟨j.val-1,by omega⟩), 1⟩
  | true => if h : j.val < s then ⟨.inr (e,leftHalf ⟨j.val,h⟩), 1⟩
      else originalSide (T.side e true)

def refine {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) (s : ℕ) :
    Diagram d (Cell V E s) (Joint d E s) where
  side
    | (e,.inl j), b => seam T s e j b
    | (e,.inr (j,i)), b =>
      ⟨.inr (e, if b then rightHalf j else leftHalf j), Equiv.swap 0 i.succ⟩

/-- The number of pillows in equation (1), truncated at zero. -/
def layers (n : ℕ) := 2 * Nat.clog 2 n - 1

/-- A zero-dimensional triangulation needs no pillows. -/
def depth (d n : ℕ) := if d = 0 then 0 else layers n

/-- The shorter stacks used for the leading constant in the abstract. -/
def shortLayers (d n : ℕ) := if d ≤ 1 ∨ n ≤ 5 then 0 else Nat.clog 2 n

end Lax919488.StackedPillows

proofs.description:
Use the stacked pillow refinement, transport the realization homeomorphism
to the given manifold, and apply the simplex count and dual-width bound.

Process the subdivided dual edges one at a time. Place the original vertices
at leaves of a binary heap and move the interior vertices of each path up
the source branch and down the target branch. At every intermediate partition
a tree node has at most 3 tree neighbors and 1 extra neighbor on the current
path. Finally contract the tree from the leaves inward.

Each pillow supplies two interior vertices, which can both be zipped directly
onto the tree. A stack with one pillow per tree level therefore suffices.
Graphs on at most 5 vertices and graphs of maximum degree at most 2 already
have twin-width at most 4.

Keep all original multiplicities between singleton parts. After a merge,
a homogeneous complete pair has one black edge, a homogeneous empty pair
has none, and a mixed pair has one red edge. These entries satisfy the
multigraph contraction rules and have the prescribed red degrees.

Cut the simplex at the source of each gluing into a smaller core and the two
halves of a pillow, keeping its other facets fixed. Iterate these cuts.
The local charts cover each old simplex and paste along exactly the specified
faces, giving inverse continuous maps on the two quotient realizations.

For $n\ge2$, the ceiling logarithm is at most the floor logarithm plus $1$.
Thus the number of layers is at most $3\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$.

For large stacks the inequality follows from the ceiling logarithm being
at most one above the floor logarithm. At the first few levels use integer
power comparisons. At $d=2$, $n=9$ the facet count gives at most 13 gluings.

Each gluing contributes $2s$ new simplices. Its two facet occurrences are
distinct from those of every other gluing, so $2m\le (d+1)n$.
Use the shorter stacks, their size estimate, and the lifted width-4 sequence.
